purpose: Manage an evidence-gathering session from question intake through retrieval, validation, conflict handling, sufficiency assessment, closure or explicit blocking, while preserving provenance and audit history.
state_transition_rules: Do not mark evidence received as validated until document identity and relevant matches are checked.
Do not mark a session sufficient merely because a retrieval succeeded.
A failed retrieval may produce a valid alternative route, but failure itself is not evidence of absence.
A conflict moves the session to conflict handling before definitive closure.
When one missing item is resolved, recompute sufficiency rather than assuming the entire profile is satisfied.
Historical sessions preserve their target date even if current records are later retrieved.
User-supplied documents remain identified as user-supplied unless independently verified.
Session closure records why the session closed and what remains unresolved.
retry_rules: Retry only when the failure is potentially recoverable.
Do not repeat an identical failed request without new information.
If identity is uncertain, improve identifiers before repeating document retrieval.
If access is restricted, route to the applicable access procedure rather than treating restriction as non-existence.
If source remains unavailable, record the limitation and identify a valid alternative if one exists.
hard_stops: Never treat retrieval success as evidential sufficiency.
Never treat retrieval failure as proof that a record does not exist.
Never silently change the property or target date to make retrieval succeed.
Never discard failed attempts, conflicts or unresolved dependencies from the session history.
Never close a material session with an unresolved conflict hidden from the final state.
